=== FIRST ===
Lecture: Lesson 1.1.2: Motion under Constant Acceleration and Free Fall

Section 1: Derivation and Application of Constant Acceleration Kinematic Equations
- Section Identity: Section 1: Derivation and Application of Constant Acceleration Kinematic Equations
- Core Understanding: When acceleration is constant (\\(a = a_c\\)), direct integration of the fundamental kinematic differential equations (\\(dv = a_c\,dt\\) and \\(ds = v\,dt\\)) yields the three primary constant-acceleration equations: \\(v = v_0 + a_c t\\), \\(s = s_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a_c t^2\\), and \\(v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a_c (s - s_0)\\). These equations are valid strictly when acceleration remains constant throughout the motion interval.
- Visual-First Explanation: An integrating calculus timeline displaying \\(a(t) = a_c\\) as a flat horizontal line. As time progresses, integrating the area under \\(a(t)\\) generates a straight rising line for \\(v(t)\\), and integrating \\(v(t)\\) generates a parabolic curve for \\(s(t)\\).
- Visual Scene Script: A dynamic graph stack displaying three synchronized plots (\\(a-t\\), \\(v-t\\), \\(s-t\\)). On the \\(a-t\\) plot, a shaded rectangular area accumulates under \\(a = a_c\\), driving the line slope on the \\(v-t\\) graph (\\(v = v_0 + a_c t\\)). Simultaneously, the area under the \\(v-t\\) curve accumulates to construct the parabolic trajectory \\(s(t) = s_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a_c t^2\\).
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive acceleration slider adjusting \\(a_c\\), instantly morphing the slope of \\(v(t)\\) and the curvature of \\(s(t)\\), with real-time integral fill area animations.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students visualize how constant acceleration transforms directly into linear velocity growth and quadratic position progression through calculus integration.
- Concept Check: Can you use \\(s = s_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2\\) if acceleration is given as \\(a = 3t + 2\\)? (Answer: No, because acceleration is variable (\\(a = f(t)\\)), so direct integration of \\(a(t)\\) must be performed instead).
- Conceptual Summary: Constant acceleration \\(a_c\\) integrates to linear velocity \\(v = v_0 + a_c t\\), quadratic position \\(s = s_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a_c t^2\\), and time-independent velocity \\(v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a_c (s - s_0)\\).
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: لما تكون العجلة ثابته (Constant acceleration \\(a = a_c\\))، بنقدر نكامل معادلات الحركة التفاضلية بشكل مباشر ونطلع الـ 3 معادلات المشهورة: الأولى \\(v = v_0 + a_c t\\)، الثانية \\(s - s_0 = v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a_c t^2\\)، والثالثة \\(v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a_c (s - s_0)\\). القوانين دي خط أحمر: ممنوع تستخدمها إطلاقاً إلا لو كانت العجلة ثابته!
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(v = v_0 + a_c t\\), \\(s = s_0 + v_0 t + \frac{1}{2} a_c t^2\\), \\(v^2 = v_0^2 + 2 a_c (s - s_0)\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: لما تكون سايق عربية ومثبت على دواسة البنزين بضغط متساوي وبمعدل تسارع ثابت، سرعتك بتزيد بانتظام كل ثانية، والمسافة اللي بتقطعها بتزيد بشكل متضاعف (تربيعي) مع الوقت.

Section 2: Vertical Motion Under Gravity (Free Fall Kinematics)
- Section Identity: Section 2: Vertical Motion Under Gravity (Free Fall Kinematics)
- Core Understanding: Free fall is a specialized rectilinear constant-acceleration motion where gravity acts vertically downward (\\(a_y = -g = -9.81\text{ m/s}^2\\) or \\(-32.2\text{ ft/s}^2\\), neglecting air resistance). Establishing a positive upward \\(y\\)-axis gives \\(v_y = v_{0y} - gt\\), \\(y = y_0 + v_{0y}t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2\\), and \\(v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 - 2g(y - y_0)\\). At peak height, vertical velocity momentarily drops to zero (\\(v_y = 0\\)).
- Visual-First Explanation: A ball tossed vertically upward from an elevated window (\\(y_0\\)). A vertical coordinate axis tracks position \\(y\\). Velocity vectors point upward and shrink to zero at peak height \\(h_{max}\\), then point downward and expand as the ball falls to the ground.
- Visual Scene Script: A ball is launched upwards at \\(v_{0y} = +10\text{ m/s}\\) from \\(y_0 = 20\text{ m}\\). A dynamic force/acceleration vector \\(-g\\) continually pulls downward. As the ball ascends, its velocity vector shortens until \\(v_y = 0\\) at apex (\\(t_{peak} = v_{0y}/g\\)). The ball then falls downward, increasing downward speed until impact at ground level (\\(y = 0\\)).
- Dynamic View Blueprint: Interactive launch velocity slider \\(v_{0y}\\) and height slider \\(y_0\\) showing live trajectory curve \\(y(t)\\), peak elevation marker, and landing time calculation.
- Visual Learning Outcome: Students master sign conventions (upward positive, acceleration \\(-g\\) downward) and key boundary conditions (\\(v_y = 0\\) at peak height).
- Concept Check: A ball thrown straight up reaches its maximum height. What are its velocity and acceleration at the apex? (Answer: Velocity \\(v = 0\text{ m/s}\\), while acceleration remains constant at \\(a = -g = -9.81\text{ m/s}^2\\) downward).
- Conceptual Summary: Free fall uses constant acceleration \\(a = -g\\); at maximum height, \\(v_y = 0\\), while acceleration remains constant throughout flight.
- شرح للجزء بالعامية المصرية: السقوط الحر أو المقذوفات الرأسية هي حالة خاصة من حركة العجلة الثابتة، بتتحرك فيها الأجسام تحت تأثير الجاذبية الأرضية فقط (\\(a = -g = -9.81\text{ m/s}^2\\)). لو فرضنا إن اتجاه فوق هو الموجب، يبقى العجلة دايماً بالسالب لأن الجاذبية بتشد لأسفل. وعند أقصى ارتفاع، سرعة الجسم اللحظية بتبقى بـ صفر (\\(v = 0\\)) بس العجلة بتفضل شغالـة وبنفس القيمة \\(-g\\)!
- القوانين (إن وُجدت): \\(v_y = v_{0y} - gt\\), \\(y = y_0 + v_{0y}t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2\\), \\(v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 - 2g(y - y_0)\\), \\(\text{At maximum height: } v_y = 0 \implies t_{peak} = \frac{v_{0y}}{g}\\)
- إسقاط على مثال أو موقف من الحياة اليومية لتثبيت الفهم: لما تحدف كورة لفوق في الهوا، الكورة بتبطأ وهي طالعة لحد ما تقف لحظياً في الجو عند أعلى نقطة، وبعدين تبدأ تنزل وتسرّع وهي نازلة بنفس معدل التسارع (\\(9.81\text{ m/s}^2\\)).
